source_inspections.evidence_extract: Reuters reported that in early Asian trading on October 19, Brent fell $1.94, or 1.77%, to $107.92 and West Texas Intermediate fell 83 cents, or 0.82%, to $100.58 after Trump waived Graham Act sanctions and tariffs. A cited analyst attributed the move to a softer sanctions tone and profit-taking, and said uncertainty over the details and duration meant markets were unlikely to price in a sustained supply increase.
